contracts.commit_point: session.run(cypher, parameters=...) at langchain-agent/tools/neo4j_client.py:44, executed within the session created at line 43 — the point where a Cypher statement would commit against the database.
contracts.declared_mechanism: run_read() opens the session with driver.session(database=get_database(), default_access_mode='READ') (neo4j_client.py:43) and executes Cypher via session.run inside that read-only session (neo4j_client.py:44), serializing and capping returned rows at the limit parameter.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Any database write (graph mutation) attempted through the tool query path — i.e., a session created by run_read() operating in a write-capable access mode, or a mutating Cypher statement committed via run_read()'s session.
pending_binding_information: Which @tool-decorated functions invoke run_read() and whether all agent-initiated Neo4j queries funnel exclusively through it (graph tool implementations such as vector_search_paragraph, get_sections, shortest_path are not supplied).
Whether any agent-reachable code path creates a Neo4j session without default_access_mode='READ' or issues write transactions outside run_read().
contracts.protected_operation: Execution of Cypher statements (with parameters and result-row limit) against the Neo4j database via run_read().
contracts.protected_resource: The Neo4j database resolved by get_database() (default 'neo4j') holding the Wikipedia snapshot graph.
contracts.protection_obligation: Agent-initiated queries against the Neo4j Wikipedia snapshot graph must execute only inside read-only database sessions: every session opened by run_read() is created with default_access_mode='READ', so no database write may commit through the tool query path.
scope_limits: The guard is anchored only in run_read() in the supplied langchain-agent/tools/neo4j_client.py; the supplied source does not show that agent tool implementations exclusively route Neo4j access through run_read().
The row cap (limit=100 default) bounds result size; it is not the write-forbidding mechanism.
The read-only guarantee applies only to sessions created by run_read(); get_driver()/get_database() connection setup itself imposes no access mode.

contracts.commit_point: The eval() call at langchain-agent/tools/calculate.py:34 — the in-process point where the expression string is executed.
contracts.declared_mechanism: eval(expression, {'__builtins__': {}}, _ALLOWED_NAMES) at calculate.py:34, where _ALLOWED_NAMES (calculate.py:10-18) maps every public attribute of the math module plus abs, round, min, max; non-string/empty expressions are rejected at calculate.py:31-32 and evaluation errors are returned as JSON error payloads (calculate.py:35-36).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Arbitrary code execution during evaluation of the expression string — i.e., the evaluated expression reaching Python builtins, dunder attributes, or any name outside _ALLOWED_NAMES.
pending_binding_information: Confirmation that deployments exposing 'calculate' always use this supplied implementation (tool selection is per-deployment, e.g., run_experiment.py:64-76).
contracts.protected_operation: Evaluation of the model-supplied 'expression' string argument inside the calculate tool (arithmetic operators, parentheses, and math-module functions per the tool docstring).
contracts.protected_resource: The Python interpreter/process executing the agent tool (the host execution environment reachable from eval).
contracts.protection_obligation: The calculate agent tool must evaluate its expression argument only via a sandboxed eval call constructed with empty builtins and a fixed name allowlist, forbidding arbitrary code execution at the eval commit point.
scope_limits: The sandbox is declared only at the eval call in langchain-agent/tools/calculate.py; resistance of this construction to specific escape techniques is a runtime property not adjudicated here.
Covers only the 'calculate' tool; no other tool's execution path is in scope.
Expression content originates from model tool-call arguments; the guard constrains the eval environment, not the syntactic content of expressions.

contracts.commit_point: The middleware wrap of each tool call wired at agent construction (langchain-agent/neo4j_agent.py:131) — over-limit calls are intercepted at the wrap point before tool execution.
contracts.declared_mechanism: ToolCallLimitMiddleware(run_limit=run_limit) placed in create_agent's middleware list (neo4j_agent.py:125-131); run_limit is threaded from create_neo4j_agent (signature default 5, neo4j_agent.py:95-101) and set to 10 in the supplied eval deployment (run_experiment.py:226-230).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A tool call attempted beyond run_limit within a single agent invocation (a runaway or infinite tool-call loop); prompts.py:62-63 states the corresponding maximum of 10 tool call rounds and that excess tool calls 'will be stopped by a tool call limit middleware'.

contracts.protected_operation: Each agent tool invocation during a run — every dispatched tool call whose execution produces downstream Neo4j/LLM/eval effects.
contracts.protected_resource: The agent run's tool-call budget and the downstream external resources tool calls reach (Neo4j database queries and LLM API endpoints).
contracts.protection_obligation: The neo4j agent's tool invocations per run must not exceed the configured budget: ToolCallLimitMiddleware(run_limit=run_limit), registered in create_agent's middleware list, must block any tool call beyond the cap, preventing runaway/infinite agent tool-call loops that would otherwise drive repeated Neo4j database queries and LLM API effects.
